- **feat(scripts,tasks,skills): pre-merge Greptile-body verdict gate (`task pr:merge-ready`)** (refs #796, refs #526) -- closes the SUCCESS-with-findings blind spot in the swarm Phase 5 -> 6 merge-readiness checklist. New `scripts/pr_merge_readiness.py` parses the Greptile rolling-summary comment **body** (not the GitHub `Greptile Review` CheckRun status) and exits non-zero when the PR is not merge-ready. The CheckRun goes green when Greptile finishes its review pass irrespective of confidence score or P0 / P1 findings; relying on it alone is what started the PR #652 merge-cascade incident against `Confidence: 3/5 + 1×P1 + 2×P2`. The script asserts: HEAD-SHA freshness (`Last reviewed commit:` markdown-link form mirrors the canonical regex from `templates/swarm-greptile-poller-prompt.md`), errored-sentinel absence (#526 `Greptile encountered an error while reviewing this PR`), `Confidence Score: X/5` parsed AND > 3, and zero P0 / P1 findings via HTML severity-badge counting (`<img alt="P0"`, `<img alt="P1"`) with a structured-section heading fallback (`### P0 findings (N)`). P2 findings are non-blocking per `skills/deft-directive-review-cycle/SKILL.md` Phase 2 Step 6 and do NOT gate the loop. The badge-count approach is robust by construction against the negation-context false positive (clean-summary phrasing `No P0 or P1 issues found` contains the literal P0 / P1 tokens, which a raw substring scan would flag -- the badges appear ONLY on actual findings). Three-state exit (0 merge-ready / 1 merge-blocked / 2 external error) matches the convention of `scripts/pr_check_protected_issues.py` (#702) and `scripts/pr_check_closing_keywords.py` (#737). New `tasks/pr.yml::merge-ready` Taskfile target wraps `uv run python scripts/pr_merge_readiness.py {{.CLI_ARGS}}` (no `sources:` / `generates:` per `conventions/task-caching.md` -- `--repo` and `--json` are user-facing flags). `skills/deft-directive-swarm/SKILL.md` Phase 5 -> 6 merge-readiness checklist gains a `!` MUST rule requiring `task pr:merge-ready -- <N>` to be invoked before each `gh pr merge` call (abort the cascade on non-zero exit) plus a `⊗` MUST NOT rule against merging on the basis of a SUCCESS Greptile CheckRun alone (the symmetric blind spot to the existing #526 NEUTRAL-CheckRun anti-pattern). Anti-Patterns block gains a corresponding bullet citing the PR #652 incident. New `tests/cli/test_pr_merge_readiness.py` (23 tests) covers parser correctness (clean body / badge findings / section-heading fallback / errored sentinel / unparseable confidence / unparseable SHA / clean-summary negation false-positive guard), gate evaluation (all combinations of failure modes + the PR #652 incident signature), short-SHA prefix matching against full HEAD SHAs, and `main()` exit codes for merge-ready / merge-blocked / no-greptile-comment / gh-failure / `--json` emit. **Atomic-shell-call rule (Mode-1 freshness window):** the swarm SKILL also gains a `!` MUST rule mandating that `task pr:merge-ready -- <N>` and `gh pr merge <N>` run in the same shell call (e.g. `task pr:merge-ready -- <N> && gh pr merge <N> --squash --delete-branch --admin`) so no time elapses between verdict and merge -- a readiness check more than ~60s stale risks Mode-1 false positives where an unrelated commit lands on master in the elapsed window, auto-rebase triggers a fresh Greptile pass, and the new pass surfaces a P1 the cached verdict did not see; plus a corresponding `⊗` MUST NOT rule against running the readiness check upstream of `gh pr merge` (e.g. as a batched cascade-prep step then merging later after intervening rebase / sub-agent dispatch / user discussion). **Lessons cross-reference:** new `## Greptile CheckRun SUCCESS != Review Approval (2026-05)` section in `meta/lessons.md` documenting the PR #652 incident as the recurrence record and the symmetric-blind-spot relationship to the existing #526 NEUTRAL-CheckRun lesson; per the Rule Authority [AXIOM] strongest-applicable-layer block in `main.md`, the entry is a short cross-reference (rule body lives in the deterministic gate + SKILL section, not duplicated in prose) -- generalizable pattern: ANY reviewer-posted CheckRun is a completion signal, not an approval signal. **Greptile P2 fix (PR #797 review):** the empty-body guard in `parse_greptile_body` switched from `if not body:` to `if not body or not body.strip():` to handle the production output of `gh api --jq '... // ""'` -- in raw mode jq emits a trailing newline for empty-string fallbacks, and with `--paginate` jq runs per-page, so a no-comment PR with N pages produces `"\n" * N`. The bare guard treated that as truthy and fell through to the SHA / confidence parsers, producing misleading "Could not parse ..." diagnostics instead of the intended "No Greptile rolling-summary comment found" message (the merge was still correctly blocked, but the diagnostic was wrong). New parametrized regression in `tests/cli/test_pr_merge_readiness.py::TestParseGreptileBody::test_whitespace_only_body_returns_not_found` covers single-newline, 2-page, 4-page, spaces, tab, and mixed-whitespace bodies; new `TestMain::test_no_greptile_comment_production_newline_exits_1` covers the CLI-level production path with both positive (intended diagnostic emitted) and negative (misleading diagnostics absent) assertions. 30 total tests now pass (23 prior + 6 whitespace + 1 production-newline).



### Changed



### Fixed

- **fix(scripts/release.py): release pipeline bypasses #747 branch gate via programmatic env-var (#867)** -- the just-shipped #747 detection-bound branch gate (`.githooks/pre-commit` -> `scripts/preflight_branch.py`, plus `.githooks/pre-push`) refused the in-flight v0.24.0 release-cut at Phase 4 Step 9 because the canonical `task release` pipeline commits release artifacts (CHANGELOG.md, ROADMAP.md, pyproject.toml, uv.lock) on master by design and the gate had no carve-out for that path. The e2e rehearsal did not catch this because the rehearsal's tmp clone is a fresh `git clone` with no `core.hooksPath` configured, so `.githooks/pre-commit` never fires inside the rehearsal -- only operator worktrees that have run `task setup` carry the hooks. The release pipeline is the canonical authorised commit-on-master path, so the fix is programmatic use of the SAME documented operator-side env-var bypass (`scripts/policy.py::ENV_BYPASS = "DEFT_ALLOW_DEFAULT_BRANCH_COMMIT"`) -- not a new bypass, just scoped use of the existing approved escape hatch. New module-level `_release_subprocess_env()` helper returns a copy of `os.environ` with `DEFT_ALLOW_DEFAULT_BRANCH_COMMIT="1"` set, suitable for passing as `env=` to `subprocess.run`/`_run_git`. `_run_git` gained an `env: dict[str, str] | None = None` kwarg defaulting to the pre-#867 behaviour (inherit caller env) so read-only invocations (`git status --porcelain`, `git tag -l`, `git ls-remote`, `git diff --cached`) keep working unchanged. Three call sites in `commit_release_artifacts` (Step 9 -- `git commit`), `create_tag` (Step 10 -- `git tag -a`, defence-in-depth in case a future tag-side hook lands), and `push_release` (Step 11 -- `git push --atomic origin <branch> <tag>`) now call `_release_subprocess_env()` and pass the result as `env=`; each call site carries a one-line `# #867:` comment explaining the bypass. The parent-process `os.environ` is intentionally NEVER mutated -- the env-var lives only in the subprocess env so a stale value cannot leak into a subsequent operator shell session. `scripts/preflight_branch.py` is intentionally untouched per the issue acceptance: the gate's behaviour is correct as-is; the release pipeline must adapt to it. New `tests/cli/test_release_branch_gate.py` (12 tests across `TestReleaseSubprocessEnv`, `TestCommitReleaseArtifactsBranchGate`, `TestCreateTagBranchGate`, `TestPushReleaseBranchGate`, `TestAllThreeMutationsCarryBypass`) mocks `subprocess.run` to capture the `env=` kwarg passed to git commit / tag / push during pipeline-helper invocations; asserts the bypass is present in each; asserts `os.environ` is byte-unchanged after each helper returns (no parent-process pollution); and the aggregate test re-discovers the mutation surface so a future refactor that adds a fourth git mutation without the bypass fails immediately. Closes #867; surfaced during the v0.24.0 release-cut session 2026-05-03 and ships in v0.24.0 to unblock the in-flight cut.

- **fix(skills/swarm): prohibit `git checkout` in another agent's worktree during post-merge cleanup (#800)** -- Phase 6 Step 3 (Update Master) of `skills/deft-directive-swarm/SKILL.md` previously described post-merge `git pull origin <base-branch>` without scoping to the merger's own worktree, which let a merging agent in a multi-worktree swarm pattern `cd` into a sibling worktree another agent owned and run `git checkout master --quiet` to perform the pull -- detaching HEAD on the other agent's branch. Recurrence record: PR #797 merge session (2026-05-01) -- Agent A owned `C:\repos\Deft\directive` on a refinement branch; Agent B (the merger) ran `cd C:\repos\Deft\directive; git checkout master --quiet` after merging its own PR. No work was lost (Agent A had pushed) but recovery was retroactive, not preventative; a future agent's working tree being dirty during the same overreach would have been a higher-severity outcome. Phase 6 Step 3 now carries a new `⊗` MUST NOT rule prohibiting `git checkout` (any branch) in a worktree the merger does not own (post-merge state-update MUST be performed via `git fetch origin <base-branch>` from the merger's OWN worktree, OR left to the human operator) plus a companion `!` MUST rule clarifying that the merger MAY remove its own worktree via `git worktree remove <path>` and delete the orphaned local feature branch via `git branch -D <branch>`, but MUST NOT alter any other worktree's HEAD or branch state. The Anti-Patterns block gains a corresponding `⊗` bullet citing the concrete `cd <other-worktree>; git checkout master --quiet` shape that triggered the recurrence. The new rules cross-reference the existing #727 Sub-Agent Role Separation companion rules earlier in Phase 6 -- #727 codifies sub-agent spawn shape; #800 codifies worktree HEAD operations, the same boundary discipline applied to a different surface. New `tests/content/test_swarm_skill.py` (12 parametrized assertions across 3 sections) regex-asserts Phase 6 Step 3 contains the canonical `⊗` rule tokens (U+2297 glyph guard against cp1252 `Γèù` mojibake), the `!` companion rule tokens, and an Anti-Patterns bullet citing PR #797 + #727 cross-reference + #800 self-citation under a `⊗` marker; mirrors the assertion pattern in `tests/content/test_skills.py` section 39 for the existing #727 Sub-Agent Role Separation tokens. Per the Rule Authority [AXIOM] strongest-applicable-layer rule, the rule body lives in the SKILL prose (no `meta/lessons.md` cross-reference in this PR -- other agents in the same Phase 1 cascade are touching that file). Closes #800.

- **fix(skills/review-cycle): re-fetch on cold-start to catch late-arriving bot reviews (#796)** -- closes the dual-source-fetch blind spot in `skills/deft-directive-review-cycle/SKILL.md` Phase 2 Step 1 where the agent's first fetch can land BEFORE the bot reviewer (Greptile) has posted its review on a freshly-opened PR. Previously the Step 1 dual-source contract (`gh pr view --comments` + MCP `get_review_comments` or `gh api` fallback, with `do_not_summarize_output: true`) correctly caught the `Comments Outside Diff` case but did not cover the cold-start path: if the agent fetched at T+30s after PR creation and Greptile lands at T+3-7min, both sources returned zero findings and Step 6 false-positively declared the PR review-clean. The Step 4 polling loop covered any cycle with a push, but the cold-start one-shot review-cycle entry path was uncovered. New `~` SHOULD rule `**Late-arriving bot review re-check:**` mandates a re-fetch after a ~60s delay before evaluating the Step 6 exit condition when the initial dual-source pass returns no bot review on the current HEAD SHA. Companion `⊗` MUST NOT rule against declaring the exit condition met based on a single empty fetch -- re-fetch at least once after a ~60s delay first. Cross-references the user-rule precedent on dual-source fetching + late-arriving bot reviews and `templates/swarm-greptile-poller-prompt.md` (which already handles this case for push-driven cycles in its loop body) so the rule's scope (cold-start one-shot entry path) is discoverable. New `tests/content/test_review_cycle_skill.py` (8 tests) regex-asserts: the `~` SHOULD rule presence + RFC2119 strength tag, canonical phrasing tokens (`re-fetch`, `60s`, `before evaluating`, `re-fetch at least once`), the `⊗` MUST NOT rule presence, the cross-reference to the poller template, and a defence-in-depth no-cp1252-mojibake guard against the `Γèù` corruption form fixed in the same cohort by PR #844. One-line cross-reference appended to `meta/lessons.md` per the Rule Authority [AXIOM] strongest-applicable-layer rule (the rule body lives in the skill, not duplicated in prose). Closes #796.

- **fix(run): run.bat now resolves the `run` Python entry point against `%~dp0` so `..\deft\run.bat <cmd>` works from any CWD on Windows (#791)** -- closes the adoption blocker where the launcher's `python.exe run %*` line at run.bat:25 resolved the bare `run` token against the caller's CWD instead of the directory of run.bat itself. Consumers who installed deft as `./deft/` and followed the documented `..\deft\run upgrade` invocation from their project root therefore saw `python.exe: can't open file 'run'` because Python looked for the script in the project root, not in `./deft/`. The field workaround (`python.exe "<full path>\deft\run" upgrade`) was undiscoverable. Single-line fix replaces `python.exe run %*` with `python.exe "%~dp0run" %*`; `%~dp0` is the canonical Windows idiom for self-relative path resolution (drive+path of the executing batch file with a trailing backslash), so resolution is now anchored at the launcher's directory regardless of the caller's CWD. Existing in-deft-repo invocations continue to work as a special case of the general rule. Surrounding Python version detection (lines 4-22) and Microsoft Store fallback (lines 28-40) preserved verbatim. New `tests/cli/test_run_bat_path.py` (Windows-conditional via `@pytest.mark.skipif(platform.system() != "Windows")`) carries two tests: a subprocess smoke test that runs `run.bat help` from a fresh `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory` and asserts `returncode == 0` (pre-fix this would fail because the empty tmpdir does not contain a `run` script), plus a static guard that reads `run.bat` and asserts the `"%~dp0run"` idiom is present AND the regression-shape `python.exe run %*` invocation is absent. Closes #791.

- **fix(cmd_doctor): require uv on PATH and surface https://docs.astral.sh/uv/ when missing; replace pre-v0.20 expected_dirs with v0.20+ canonical layout (#792)** -- closes the adoption blocker where `deft/run doctor` reported green on a fresh machine without `uv` installed and then every `task <name>` invocation failed with the opaque `uv: command not found` (every deft task script runs via `uv run python ...`). Two coordinated changes in `run::cmd_doctor`: (1) new required `check_command("uv", "uv (Astral Python runner)", required=True, install_url="https://docs.astral.sh/uv/")` invocation runs first so the failure is the first thing a fresh-machine user sees, plus a new module-level `_check_uv_available()` helper wrapping `shutil.which("uv")` so #793's `task migrate:preflight` aggregate can reuse the detection seam without duplicating the lookup (the install URL pointer mirrors `skills/deft-directive-setup/SKILL.md` § Environment Preflight); the inner `check_command` helper gained an `install_url=""` keyword arg so the URL pointer threads through both required and optional surfaces consistently. (2) `expected_dirs` rewritten from the pre-v0.20 list (`core, languages, interfaces, tools, swarm, templates, meta`) to the v0.20+ canonical layout (`languages, strategies, skills, templates, tasks, scripts, vbrief`), eliminating the spurious `Missing directory: <name>/` warnings the legacy entries produced on every clean checkout. Internal counters split into `errors` and `warnings` so a missing required tool (uv or git) surfaces as a `System check failed with N error(s)` summary above optional-tool warnings AND forces a non-zero exit code for CI clarity; the all-clean and warnings-only paths return the existing exit shape unchanged. New `tests/cli/test_cmd_doctor.py` (6 tests) covers `_check_uv_available` true/false branches, the uv-present and uv-missing cmd_doctor paths (asserting non-zero exit, install URL pointer, and `System check failed` summary on the uv-missing branch), zero `Missing directory:` lines against the live framework checkout (regression guard for the v0.20+ layout), and a defence-in-depth assertion that no pre-v0.20 directory name (`core`, `interfaces`, `tools`, `swarm`, `meta`) appears in the success-line output. The TUI `DoctorScreen` carries a parallel copy of the same legacy `expected_dirs` list and was intentionally left untouched as out-of-scope per the brief boundary -- a follow-up can lift the same fix into the TUI surface. Closes #792.

- **fix(scripts/release.py): refuse early when target tag exists locally, on origin, or as a published GitHub release (#784)** -- closes the adoption blocker where the legacy 12-step release pipeline only invoked `git tag` at Step 9, after Steps 1-8 had already promoted CHANGELOG to `[<version>]`, regenerated ROADMAP, synced `pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock`, built `dist/deft-<version>.zip`, and made a `chore(release): v<version>` commit locally. A duplicate-tag failure at Step 9 stranded the operator with an unpushed wrong-version commit + orphaned dist artifact + manual `git reset --hard origin/master` recovery (forbidden by AGENTS.md SCM rules without explicit permission). Surfaced 2026-05-01 during the v0.23.0 release attempt where the operator typed `0.22.0` (the prior release from 12 hours earlier); the pipeline ran 8 steps before failing at `fatal: tag 'v0.22.0' already exists`. New `check_tag_available(version, repo, project_root)` helper in `scripts/release.py` is a read-only pre-flight that probes three surfaces in order, short-circuiting on first conflict so the FAIL reason names the conflict source: (1) `git tag -l v<version>` (local tag); (2) `git ls-remote --tags origin refs/tags/v<version>` (remote tag on origin -- catches the case where the operator's fetch hasn't run); (3) `gh release view v<version> --repo <owner>/<repo> --json tagName` (published GitHub release -- catches the case where a tag was created via `gh release create` directly without a corresponding ref under `refs/tags/`). Each FAIL reason includes the actionable hint `choose a different version (operator typo of a prior release is the most likely cause)`. The `gh` CLI not on PATH is intentionally NOT a FAIL: the helper passes with an `UNVERIFIED` caveat in the reason (parallel to `verify_release_draft` (#724) gh-missing path) so the local + remote git surfaces still gate the gate even on gh-less hosts; `FileNotFoundError` / `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` from the gh probe are mapped to the same `UNVERIFIED` carve-out per the issue body's explicit `gh-CLI not-found != release-exists` contract. Wired into Phase 1 pre-flight as the new Step 4 (between vBRIEF lifecycle sync at Step 3 and CI at Step 5), so a duplicate-tag failure halts BEFORE any state mutation -- CHANGELOG promotion, ROADMAP refresh, build, commit. Pipeline-step constant `_TOTAL_STEPS` bumps 12 -> 13 (every subsequent label / dry-run preview shifts by one); existing `tests/cli/test_release.py` / `test_release_summary.py` / `test_release_vbrief_lifecycle.py` pipeline-step assertions renumbered accordingly (mirrors the 11 -> 12 shift from #734). Dry-run reports `[4/13] Pre-flight tag availability... DRYRUN (would verify v<version> tag not present locally / on origin / as GitHub release on <repo>)`; production reports `[4/13] Pre-flight tag availability... OK (...)` on clean state, `FAIL (<reason>)` with operator-actionable recovery on conflict. New `tests/cli/test_release_tag_availability.py` (15 tests across `TestCheckTagAvailableHelper`, `TestPipelineStep4`, `TestTotalStepsConstant`) covers clean state OK; local-only / remote-only / GitHub-release-only conflict each FAIL with the named surface; combinations short-circuit on first surface (local before remote before gh); gh-CLI-not-found != release-exists carve-out (both `_resolve_gh()` returning None AND `subprocess.run` raising `FileNotFoundError` paths); local + ls-remote git failures surfaced verbatim with `git tag -l failed: ...` / `git ls-remote failed: ...` reasons; pipeline Step 4 OK proceeds to Step 5 (CI); Step 4 FAIL returns `EXIT_VIOLATION` and never reaches CI; dry-run NEVER invokes the helper (read-only contract is a label-only preview); `_TOTAL_STEPS == 13` constant. `skills/deft-directive-release/SKILL.md` Phase 1 gains a new `!` MUST rule citing this issue and the v0.22.0 -> v0.23.0 incident as recurrence record plus a corresponding `⊗` MUST NOT anti-pattern. Closes #784.

- **fix(scripts/preflight_branch.py): UTF-8 self-reconfigure at hook entry to unblock Windows cp1252 commits (#814)** -- closes the HOT Windows adoption blocker where the #747 detection-bound branch gate (installed by `task setup` as `.githooks/pre-commit` + `.githooks/pre-push`) crashed with `UnicodeEncodeError: 'charmap' codec can't encode character '\u2713'` whenever the user's Python stdout defaulted to `cp1252` (the Windows default with `PYTHONIOENCODING` unset). Crucially: the gate had ALREADY APPROVED the commit before the success-path print failed, so the user saw a Python traceback after a successful check, git aborted the commit, and the workaround (`PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 git commit ...`) was undiscoverable. New main()-entry block in `scripts/preflight_branch.py` calls `sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")` (and stderr) BEFORE any print, guarded by `hasattr(..., "reconfigure")` so the call is a no-op on non-`TextIOWrapper` streams (e.g. when stdout is captured by `PIPE`). `errors='replace'` is the belt-and-suspenders fallback so a rare environment that still cannot render UTF-8 sees a printable replacement char rather than an unhandled traceback. **Audit:** `.githooks/pre-commit` and `.githooks/pre-push` both invoke exactly one script under `scripts/` (`scripts/preflight_branch.py`), so the audit surface is fully covered by the single fix; a defence-in-depth audit test re-discovers the hook-invoked surface from `.githooks/` at test time and asserts every script reference is registered against the contract -- a future hook script that lands without the reconfigure block fails immediately. New `tests/cli/test_hooks_encoding.py` (2 tests) pins the contract: a strict `cp1252` `TextIOWrapper` cannot encode U+2713 (sanity); `preflight_branch.main(["--project-root", str(tmp_path)])` invoked under that fake stdout (with `DEFT_SETUP_INTERVIEW=1`) returns 0 cleanly, `sys.stdout.encoding == "utf-8"` after main() runs, and the U+2713 glyph reaches the underlying buffer as canonical UTF-8 bytes (`b'\xe2\x9c\x93'`). **`task setup` advisory:** new informational warning surfaces when `task setup` detects a Python interpreter whose stdout defaults to a Windows code page (`cp1252` / `cp437` / `charmap`); the probe explicitly unsets `PYTHONUTF8` / `PYTHONIOENCODING` in its subshell so it measures what Python would do under git's hook environment (not the Taskfile root `env: PYTHONUTF8: "1"`). Auto-set of `PYTHONIOENCODING` is intentionally NOT done -- mutating the user's environment would surprise other tooling (out-of-scope per the issue body); the warning points at one-time `System Properties > Environment Variables` or PowerShell-profile-level fixes. New `## Windows cp1252 stdout default breaks non-ASCII prints (2026-05)` entry in `meta/lessons.md` codifies the recurring class as a short cross-reference per the Rule Authority [AXIOM] strongest-applicable-layer rule -- the rule body lives in the script + the contract test, prose is fallback only. The success glyph is intentionally preserved as `\u2713` per the issue's Out-of-Scope (fix the encoding, not the UX). Closes #814.

- **fix(vbrief): replace `Γèù` mojibake with canonical `⊗` in #796 / #800 pending briefs (PR #844 review-cycle)** -- Greptile P1 review on PR #844 surfaced 12 occurrences of the cp1252-corrupted prohibition marker (`Γèù` instead of `⊗`) in the two newly-ingested briefs `vbrief/pending/2026-05-03-796-review-cycle-dual-source-fetch-can-miss-late-arriving-bot-re.vbrief.json` (7) and `vbrief/pending/2026-05-03-800-swarm-skill-prohibit-git-checkout-in-a-worktree-another-agen.vbrief.json` (5). A swarm agent following either brief verbatim would have written `Γèù MUST NOT ...` into the target SKILL.md, failing the content-test assertions the briefs themselves prescribe. - **fix(skills,scripts): structural preflight gate prevents unauthorized implementation-agent spawn (#810)** -- closes the implementation-intent-inference adoption blocker where agents reading AGENTS.md inferred implementation intent from lifecycle / branching / PR-process language and spawned code-writing sub-agents without explicit action-verb authorization (the #801-session reproduction was the surfacing event). New `scripts/preflight_implementation.py` is a structural fail-closed gate: takes `--vbrief-path <path>`, exits 0 only when the vBRIEF lives in `vbrief/active/` AND `plan.status == "running"`, exits 1 with the actionable `task vbrief:activate <path>` redirect on every other state (pre-activation folder, wrong status, malformed JSON, missing keys, unreadable file). Pure stdlib, mirrors the `scripts/preflight_branch.py` (#747) shape: `evaluate(path) -> (code, msg)` separated from CLI plumbing for testability, `--json` variant for machine consumers. New `scripts/vbrief_activate.py` is the lifecycle move that satisfies the gate: idempotent (already-active -> no-op, exit 0), validates source is in `vbrief/pending/`, flips `plan.status` from `pending`/`approved` to `running`, stamps `vBRIEFInfo.updated` to current ISO 8601 UTC, atomically moves to `vbrief/active/` via `Path.replace`. New `tasks/vbrief.yml::activate` Taskfile target dispatches the helper with `dir: '{{.USER_WORKING_DIR}}'` consistent with the rest of the lifecycle tasks; no `sources:`/`generates:` per `conventions/task-caching.md`. `skills/deft-directive-build/SKILL.md` gains a new `Step 0 -- Implementation Preflight` section near the top with `!` rules pointing at the helper and the activate task plus `⊗` rules against inferring intent from workflow-shape vocabulary or treating affirmative continuation phrases as implementation authorization; matching anti-pattern entry added. `skills/deft-directive-swarm/SKILL.md` Phase 0 Step 1 deduplicates its inline `active/`-only check by delegating to the helper, surfaces preflight rejections in the Phase 0 Step 4 analysis, and adds a `⊗` rule against spawning agents that haven't passed the gate. New `tests/cli/test_preflight_implementation.py` (24 tests) covers the (folder, status) matrix across `proposed`/`pending`/`active`/`completed`/`cancelled`, edge cases (nonexistent path, directory path, malformed JSON, top-level not-an-object, missing plan, missing/non-string `plan.status`), `--json` schema (stable keys: `ready`/`exit_code`/`vbrief_path`/`message`), main() exit codes + stderr redirect on reject, and the recursively-appropriate self-test asserting the #810 vBRIEF in `vbrief/pending/` is itself rejected by the gate it introduces. New `tests/cli/test_vbrief_activate.py` (15 tests) covers happy path / idempotent no-op / atomic-move durability / collision detection / malformed input. New `tests/content/test_skills_preflight_call.py` regex-asserts both the build and swarm skills carry the `!` MUST line referencing `scripts/preflight_implementation.py` AND the `task vbrief:activate` redirect; failure messages cite file + missing pattern.

- **fix(templates,agents): Implementation Intent Gate documented in AGENTS.md managed-section, propagated by cmd_agents_refresh (#810)** -- prompt-side guardrail companion to the structural fix. New `## Development Process` / `### Implementation Intent Gate (#810)` block lands inside the existing `<!-- deft:managed-section v1 -->` ... `<!-- /deft:managed-section -->` markers in `templates/agents-entry.md` so `cmd_agents_refresh` (#768) propagates it to consumer projects on next refresh; managed-section markers preserved byte-stably (the existing `tests/content/test_agents_entry_contract.py` `test_render_is_byte_stable` assertion continues to pass). Same four-bullet block mirrored in repo-level `AGENTS.md` so the framework dogfoods its own template. The four bullets cover: (a) `!` MUST run `scripts/preflight_implementation.py` before any code-writing tool call; (b) `!` MUST require explicit action-verb directive (`build`/`implement`/`ship`/`swarm`/`run agents`/`start agent`) before invoking the gate; (c) `⊗` MUST NOT infer implementation intent from lifecycle/branching/PR-process language; (d) `⊗` MUST NOT treat affirmative continuation phrases (`yes`/`go`/`proceed`/`do it`) as implementation authorization unless the prior turn explicitly proposed implementation. New tests in `tests/content/test_agents_entry_contract.py` (3 tests) assert the managed-section contains the `Implementation Intent Gate` anchor, the gate region carries at least 4 bullets, and the prefix-token mix is at least 2 `!` AND at least 2 `⊗`; structure/tokens are pinned, not exact wording, so future copy-edits don't break the contract. New `## Implementation-intent inference is a documented anti-pattern (#810)` entry in `meta/lessons.md` codifies the failure mode (trigger phrases like "do the full PR process", "poller agents not local loops" parsed as implementation authorization), the structural gate as the mitigation, and the takeaway that workflow-shape vocabulary is NOT authorization. Closes #810.

Four phases: read the spec & detect categories; draft the artifact; read it back to the user; decision point. Discuss, 6. Back). Skill carries the canonical RFC2119 legend, a Platform Detection block (Windows `%APPDATA%\deft\USER.md` / Unix `~/.config/deft/USER.md` / `$DEFT_USER_PATH` override) mirroring `skills/deft-directive-build/SKILL.md`, an Inputs block, an Output Targets block, an Anti-Patterns block, and an `## EXIT` block per the AGENTS.md Skill Completion Gate. USD-only first pass; vendor pricing snapshots cited as snapshots, never guarantees; loose ranges only (no single-point estimates). (3) **NEW `references/cost-models.md`** -- captures the cost-model methodology (loose ranges, no hard numbers, USD-only first pass; documented as such). Five coordinated changes share one principle -- the gate is upgrade-path-agnostic, the framework owns the AGENTS.md contract, UPGRADING.md is the only source of truth per state. (1) New `cmd_gate` in `run` -- read-only state-vector probe emitting `OK v<current>` or `NEEDS-UPGRADE recorded=<recorded|unknown> current=<current> precutover=<csv|empty> agents-md=<current|stale|missing|absent>` with `--json` variant; reuses `_read_version_marker`, `_detect_pre_cutover_legacy`, `_running_inside_deft_repo`, dynamic `VERSION` (#741); no marker writes, no migrations, no commits; the `agents-md=` axis is computed via `_classify_agents_md` against the rendered template. (2) New `cmd_agents_refresh` in `run` -- Python reference implementation of the AGENTS.md contract; `--dry-run` shows the planned change, `--check` exits 0 only when the consumer's managed section is byte-identical to the rendered template; reads `templates/agents-entry.md`, handles four states (`current` / `stale` / `missing` / `absent`); legacy-to-marker migration on first run preserves consumer notes above the bracketed region. `cmd_upgrade` now calls `cmd_agents_refresh` automatically alongside writing `vbrief/.deft-version`. (3) Universal `<!-- DEFT-PREAMBLE-V1 -->` preamble injected at line 1 of `main.md` plus every legacy redirect stub enumerated by the `git --no-pager log --all -- cmd/deft-install/setup.go` audit (`skills/deft-setup/SKILL.md`, `skills/deft-build/SKILL.md`, root `SKILL.md`); the preamble instructs the agent to run `python3 deft/run gate` before any other instruction in the file and on non-zero exit to read `deft/UPGRADING.md` and follow the section whose `Applies when` clause matches the printed state vector, honoring any `Restart required` directive. (4) Contract artifacts: `<!-- deft:managed-section v1 --> ... <!-- /deft:managed-section -->` markers added to `templates/agents-entry.md` (versioned for future format detection); new `templates/agents-entry.placeholders.md` documents the placeholder spec (`UPSTREAM_SHA`, `UPSTREAM_REF`, `UPSTREAM_TAG`, `FETCHED_AT`, `FETCHED_BY` -- inherited from the webinstaller pin-marker contract); rail-agnostic conformance test `tests/content/test_agents_entry_contract.py` asserts the template parses, placeholders match the spec, markers are well-formed, and byte-identical refresh produces byte-identical output. (5) UPGRADING.md retrofit: every `## From <prev> -> <new>` section now carries the four-field micro-format header (`Applies when` / `Safe to auto-run` / `Restart required` / `Commands`); `tests/content/test_upgrading_sections.py` enforces the contract going forward. ### Changed

- **feat(skills,interview): plain-English UX pass -- jargon, approval menus, diff preface (#740, refs #151 playtest umbrella, refs #767 deterministic-questions framework rule)** -- closes the consumer-adoption defect cluster surfaced by the #151 playtest where non-technical users only completed the planning flow because they had a second AI translating jargon, decoding ambiguous approval actions, and explaining red/green diffs. Three coordinated UX rules across `skills/deft-directive-interview/SKILL.md` and `strategies/interview.md`: (1) **Jargon pass** -- every technical question MUST carry a one-line plain-English context note as preamble above the structured-tool call (per Rule 2 Preamble Placement), every acronym MUST be defined inline on first use (`PRD (Product Requirements Document)`, `NFR`, `FR`, `SPEC`, `API`, `DB`, `CI`, `MVP`), and every framework recommendation MUST either explain the rationale in plain-English terms the user actually cares about (cost, speed, hiring, hosting compatibility) OR remove the rationale entirely and present it as an overridable default -- one-word `industry-standard` / `modern` / `scalable` justifications are a ⊗ anti-pattern. (2) **Approval-menu pass** -- explicit numbered approval menu after PRD review AND after SPEC review with action-shaped labels (`1. Approve and continue` / `2. Suggest changes` / `3. Edit yourself` / `4. Discuss` / `5. Back`). The menus follow the **#767 deterministic-questions framework rule**: the final two numbered options MUST be `Discuss` and `Back`, in that order. The framework rule itself is being landed by Agent 1 in #767; this PR cross-references it with a `!` MUST cross-reference at every menu site so once `contracts/deterministic-questions.md` exists this surface defers to it for canonical wording. (3) **Diff-view preface pass** -- when a PRD or SPECIFICATION review surfaces a red/green diff, the agent MUST emit a one-line non-alarming preface above it (`Here's what changed since the previous draft. Red lines were removed, green lines were added. Nothing here is broken -- this is a normal review.`) OR hide the diff entirely on the first review pass and present a plain-English summary instead. New `references/plain-english-ux.md` codifies all six rules (plain-English context note, acronyms-on-first-use, framework justifications explained-or-removed, numbered approval menu with Discuss/Back final-two per #767, diff-view preface, audience test) plus canonical PRD-review and SPECIFICATION-review approval menus and an Anti-Patterns block. Tests: 30 content tests in `tests/content/test_plain_english_ux.py` covering reference-doc rule presence, acronym-on-first-use rule named in interview surfaces, approval-menu presence (PRD + SPEC), diff-preface presence (skill + strategy PRD section + strategy SPEC section), Discuss/Back-final-two assertion via regex extractor that walks numbered-menu blocks and checks `menu[-2]` contains `Discuss` and `menu[-1]` contains `Back` on every approval menu in interview SKILL + interview strategy + reference doc canonical menus, and #767 cross-reference assertions. Closes #740.

- **fix(tasks/core.yml,scripts/build_dist.py): cross-platform `task build` artifact parity (#736)** -- the prior `tasks/core.yml::build` shape dispatched `tar -czf ... --exclude=...` on linux/darwin and `powershell -NoProfile -Command "Compress-Archive -Path . -DestinationPath dist\deft-X.Y.Z.zip -Force"` on windows. The Windows branch had no exclude list so the produced zip ingested `.git/` (often hundreds of MB of history), `backup/`, `node_modules/`, AND -- because `Compress-Archive -Path .` walks the output directory recursively -- the prior `dist/` artifact, leading to unbounded growth on every re-run. CI never caught this because no test asserted shape parity across the platform branches. New `scripts/build_dist.py` (stdlib-only via `tarfile` / `zipfile`) replaces the platform split with a single Python helper that uses one canonical exclude list (`.git`, `dist`, `backup`, `node_modules`, plus the Python-tooling caches `__pycache__`, `.venv`, `htmlcov`, `.pytest_cache`, `.mypy_cache`, `.ruff_cache`, `.coverage`), auto-selects `tar.gz` on Linux/macOS and `zip` on Windows (overridable via `--format`), and accepts an optional `--exclude-extra` flag to extend the canonical set. Idempotent re-run is guaranteed structurally by including `dist` in the canonical exclude list -- a stale prior artifact at `dist/deft-<version>.<ext>` cannot be ingested because the directory is pruned during `os.walk` traversal. `tasks/core.yml::build` now dispatches a single `uv run python {{.DEFT_ROOT}}/scripts/build_dist.py --version {{.VERSION}}` command (no platform split); the same simplification lands on `tasks/core.yml::clean` (replaces the `rm -rf dist/` + `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force dist` duplication with a single `uv run python -c "import shutil, pathlib; ..."` command using `shutil.rmtree`). New `tests/cli/test_build_dist.py` (parametrized over linux-tar / windows-zip / macos-tar) covers excluded-path correctness, expected-core-paths-present (`scripts/`, `skills/`, `tasks/`, `AGENTS.md`), 50 MB sanity ceiling, idempotent re-run (with a marker file added between runs to make regression visible), `--exclude-extra` flag, CLI surface (argparse, three-state exit codes), and an end-to-end smoke test that invokes `task build` against the real repo (skipped when `task` is not on PATH; mirrors the pattern in `tests/content/test_taskfile_caching.py` and `tests/content/test_taskfile_release_names.py`). New `tests/content/test_taskfile_zip_parity.py` parses `tasks/core.yml` and asserts the `build` task uses a single cross-platform command with no `cmds[].platforms` entries, dispatches via `scripts/build_dist.py`, and is collapsed to <=2 cmds; mirror assertions guard the `clean` task's simplification (no `platforms:` split, no `powershell`, no `rm -rf`). Closes #736.

Report may be incomplete.` and silently excluded older issues from dedup/coverage. ## [0.22.0] - 2026-04-30



> Release-pipeline trust: lifecycle-gate scaling + draft auto-flip and VERSION drift fixes. Plus pre-PR/CLI gates, README cleanup, and pytest+pygments security bumps.



### Added

- **feat(cli): enforce USER.md gate in `cmd_spec` and `cmd_project` (#163)** -- mirror the agentic-path USER.md gate documented in `skills/deft-directive-build/SKILL.md` ("USER.md Gate" section) at the two CLI entry points that consume user-scoped defaults. Two new helpers in `run`: `_resolve_user_md_path()` resolves USER.md per platform (Windows: `%APPDATA%\deft\USER.md`; Unix: `~/.config/deft/USER.md`) with `$DEFT_USER_PATH` always taking precedence on any platform; `_check_user_md_gate()` returns `1` and emits a `print_error` redirect ("USER.md not found at <path>", "Run 'run bootstrap' to create your user preferences before continuing.", "Set $DEFT_USER_PATH to override the default location.") when USER.md is missing, or `None` to let the caller continue. `cmd_spec` and `cmd_project` invoke the gate before any prompts or work so a missing USER.md exits non-zero with an actionable message instead of silently generating a scope vBRIEF / PROJECT-DEFINITION that lacks the user defaults (languages, coverage, strategy) downstream tooling depends on. The gate intentionally lives at the function entry (not in `main()`'s dispatcher) so `cmd_install` and `cmd_bootstrap`'s post-success chain into `cmd_project` / `cmd_spec` go through the same check. New `tests/cli/test_usermd_gate.py` (9 tests) covers all three plan.items from `vbrief/active/2026-04-23-163-...vbrief.json`: resolver honors `$DEFT_USER_PATH` override; `_check_user_md_gate()` returns `None` when present and `1` when missing (with redirect message asserted via `capsys`); `cmd_spec` and `cmd_project` both block at the gate when USER.md is missing (asserts non-zero exit, no output file written, message names the resolved path AND `run bootstrap`); both commands proceed normally when USER.md is present at the resolved path; both commands honor the `$DEFT_USER_PATH` override against a custom tmp_path location -- bypassing the standard `isolated_env*` fixtures so the developer's real USER.md is never touched. New `tests/cli/conftest.py` overrides the parent `isolated_env` fixture (defined in `tests/conftest.py`) to additionally pre-create a minimal USER.md at `$DEFT_USER_PATH` so existing CLI tests (cmd_spec / cmd_project happy paths in `test_cmd_spec.py`, `test_project.py`, `test_spec_sizing.py`, `test_loop_bugs.py::test_project_*`, `test_project_user_defaults.py`) keep passing without per-test edits; sibling `isolated_env_no_user` fixture exposes the absence path for the new gate tests, the gate-flip in `test_project_user_defaults.py::test_project_blocks_when_user_md_missing` (replaces the prior `test_project_still_works_without_user_md` whose semantics inverted with this change), the `test_read_user_defaults_returns_none_when_missing` unit test, and the `cmd_bootstrap` tests in `test_bootstrap.py` / `test_resume.py` / `test_loop_bugs.py::test_bootstrap_*` (which write USER.md as their primary behavior under test). `task check` green (2983 passed, 1 xfailed). Scope vBRIEF: `vbrief/active/2026-04-23-163-enforce-user-md-gate-in-cli-path-parity-with-agentic.vbrief.json`. Closes #163.

- **feat(scripts,skills): vBRIEF-lifecycle reconciliation gate (#734)** -- new `--apply-lifecycle-fixes` flag on `scripts/reconcile_issues.py` moves Section (c) (closed-issue) vBRIEFs from `proposed/` / `pending/` / `active/` into `completed/`, sets `plan.status = "completed"`, and stamps `vBRIEFInfo.updated`; idempotent on re-run; tolerant of both legacy bare `github-issue` and canonical `x-vbrief/github-issue` reference shapes; reverse mismatches (vBRIEFs in `completed/` whose origin issue reopened) are reported via the existing reconcile output but never auto-reverse-moved (operator decision per the vBRIEF). New `scripts/release.py::check_vbrief_lifecycle_sync(project_root, repo)` helper wraps the same `reconcile_issues` surface and is wired into the release pipeline as a brand-new Step 3 between branch guard (Step 2) and CI (Step 4); the helper returns a three-state result (clean / mismatch-fail / config-error) and the pipeline emits `[3/12] Pre-flight vBRIEF lifecycle sync... OK|FAIL|SKIP|DRYRUN` lines so operators can tail the run. The pipeline-step constant `_TOTAL_STEPS` bumps 11 -> 12 (every subsequent label / dry-run preview shifts by one); existing test_release.py / test_release_summary.py pipeline-step assertions are renumbered accordingly. ### Fixed

- fix(release): vBRIEF-lifecycle-sync gate now scales by vBRIEF-referenced-issue-count, not repo-open-issue-count -- inverted lookup via batched gh api graphql retires the 200-issue pagination cap and the Tier 2 truncation-guard surface (#754)

- **fix(scripts/release_e2e.py): pass `--allow-vbrief-drift` to dispatched `task release` against the auto-created temp repo** (post-#754 harness fix, refs #720 e2e harness, refs #734 lifecycle gate). The temp rehearsal repo is created empty (zero issues), so the inverted-lookup vBRIEF-lifecycle-sync gate from #754 classifies every referenced issue number as NOT_FOUND -> Section (c) mismatch and the inner pipeline fails at Step 3. The escape hatch is the correct surface to bypass the gate in the rehearsal context; the production cut path against a real repo does NOT pass this flag and remains fully gated. Latent since #734 landed (April 29) -- the v0.21.0 cut session never ran `task release:e2e` post-#734, so the regression surfaced today during the v0.22.0 Phase 3 e2e gate. `tests/cli/test_release_e2e.py::TestDispatchTaskRelease::test_argv_carries_allow_vbrief_drift` regression-guards the flag.

- **fix(.github/workflows/release.yml): release job no longer auto-flips draft -> public** (#733, refs #716): The workflow's `release` job ran `softprops/action-gh-release@v2` without `draft: true`, and the action defaults `draft` to `false` -- so every tag push silently flipped the GitHub release from draft (created locally by `task release`) to public, bypassing the #716 Phase 5 user-only authority gate. Fix sets `draft: true` explicitly on the softprops step so the workflow becomes BUILD AND UPLOAD only and `task release:publish` remains the sole authorised path that flips draft -> public. New `tests/content/test_release_workflow.py` parses `.github/workflows/release.yml` and asserts no softprops usage with `draft: false` or unset, no `gh release edit --draft=false` step, and no other isDraft-flipping pattern (defensive regex scan for `"draft": false` JSON bodies and `is_draft: false` aliases). Also adds a new `verify-run-version` job in the same workflow per #741 (separate `### Fixed` entry below) that fails the release on a tag push when `run`'s resolved VERSION disagrees with the pushed tag, closing the regression loop for future drift.

- **fix(run, .github/workflows/release.yml): dynamic VERSION resolution in `run`; CI assertion against pushed tag** (#741, refs #723 sibling Taskfile-side dynamic resolver, refs #74 / #716 release foundation): The hard-coded `VERSION = "X.Y.Z"` literal in `run` was the root cause of the v0.21.0 stale-version incident -- nothing in the release pipeline updated the literal, so `run --help` reported `0.20.0` for weeks after the v0.21.0 tag landed. Path A (locked per swarm-prep) removes the literal entirely. The replacement is an inline priority chain mirroring `scripts/resolve_version.py::resolve_version()`: (1) `$DEFT_RELEASE_VERSION` env override (set by `scripts/release.py::run_build` so `task release -- 0.X.Y` pins the in-flight version); (2) `git describe --tags --abbrev=0` with leading `v` stripped (ordinary tagged checkouts); (3) `0.0.0-dev` fallback for fresh checkouts with no tags or repositories where `git` is unavailable. The chain is intentionally inlined rather than imported from `scripts/resolve_version.py` because `run` is the framework's bootstrap entry point -- the two implementations are kept in lockstep by convention and pinned by parallel regression coverage. `.github/workflows/release.yml` gains a `verify-run-version` job that fetches full tag history, imports `run` to resolve VERSION via the priority chain, and fails the workflow on tag push if the resolved value disagrees with `${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}` -- defence against future drift regardless of which fix path was taken. New `tests/cli/test_run_version.py` (14 tests across `TestPriorityChain`, `TestNoLiteralVersion`, and a smoke test) cover env override / git tag stripping / dev fallback / priority order / whitespace handling AND a forbid-the-literal guard scan of `run` source so the regression cannot recur. Tests live in a sibling module rather than extending `tests/cli/test_release.py` because that file is already 1771 lines (over the AGENTS.md 1000-line MUST limit), mirroring the established `test_release_skip_flags.py` / `test_release_summary.py` split-out pattern.

- **feat(scripts,tasks,skills,docs): release safety hardening (#716, refs #74 foundation, refs #233 More Determinism umbrella, refs #642 workflow umbrella, refs #635 epic anchor, refs #709 Repair Authority [AXIOM] -- this PR demonstrates the rule by landing the safety net atomically with the foundation rather than deferring to a follow-up, refs #710 data-file-conventions follow-up, refs #633 pre-PR deterministic CI enforcement umbrella)**: Expands the `task release` foundation (Item below) with the full safety net per the canonical [#716 spec](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/716), so master never enters a "release-without-rollback" state. Seven coordinated artifacts: (1) `scripts/release.py` defaults `gh release create` to `--draft` and exposes `--no-draft` for the rare direct-publish case (e.g. automated security patches); the Step-10 pipeline label suffixes `(draft)` / `(PUBLIC)` and the dry-run preview surfaces `--draft` in the operator-readable plan -- this decouples the *artifact production* phase (release.yml CI + binary upload) from the *consumer-visibility* phase. (2) `scripts/release_publish.py` + `task release:publish -- <version>` flips a draft to public via `gh release edit --draft=false`; four-state machine (`draft` -> proceed; already-`published` -> exit 0 no-op; `not-found` -> exit 1; `gh-error` -> exit 1) with a post-edit re-read verifying `isDraft` actually flipped (catches stale-cache / silent-noop / wrong-tag cases). (3) `scripts/release_rollback.py` + `task release:rollback -- <version>` performs a state-aware unwind across four detected states (local commit + tag, tag pushed no release, release published with downloads <= guard, release published with downloads > guard) with a **time-windowed download-count guard** per #716 Q3 (release age < 5 min -> threshold = 0; 5-30 min -> threshold = max(--allow-low-downloads, 10) to filter bot fetches; > 30 min -> refuse without --allow-data-loss because downloads are likely consumer-driven), three escape hatches (`--allow-low-downloads N`, `--allow-data-loss`, `--force-strict-0` for security-incident hot-rollbacks), and a **race-condition double-read** of `download_count` (read, sleep 5s, re-read; only proceed if both reads agree below threshold -- catches a real consumer download arriving between the probe and the unwind, since GitHub's release-asset cache has ~30s staleness). (4) `scripts/release_e2e.py` + `task release:e2e` rehearses the full pipeline against an **auto-created + auto-destroyed temp GitHub repo** per #716 Q1 (`gh repo create --private deftai/deftai-release-test-<timestamp>-<uuid6>` -> rehearsal -> `gh repo delete --yes` in a `try/finally` clause so cleanup ALWAYS runs, even when the rehearsal failed; cleanup-failure surfaces a one-line manual-cleanup hint as a WARN and preserves the rehearsal exit code -- operator never sees "rehearsal succeeded" reported as "cleanup failed"); `--keep-repo` skips destroy for manual debugging; `--dry-run` invokes no gh helpers. (5) `skills/deft-directive-release/SKILL.md` + `.agents/skills/deft-directive-release/SKILL.md` thin pointer carry the **8-phase workflow** that operationalizes the entire surface: Phase 1 pre-flight (base branch, clean tree, version-bump magnitude vs CHANGELOG content, `task ci:local`, `gh auth status`); Phase 2 dry-run review with user-gate `yes`/`back`/`quit` mirroring `deft-directive-review-cycle`; Phase 3 e2e sanity against a temp repo; Phase 4 production draft via `task release -- <ver>`; Phase 5 user-only-authority draft review gate (`publish` / `rollback` / `defer`); Phase 6 branches on the user choice; Phase 7 post-publish verification (closing-keyword Layer 1 + Layer 3 reopen sweep, binary download check, ROADMAP correctness); Phase 8 generates the Slack release announcement re-using the canonical block from `skills/deft-directive-swarm/SKILL.md` Phase 6 Step 5 (single source of truth). (6) `AGENTS.md` skill-routing entry maps `"release"` / `"cut release"` / `"v0.X.Y"` / `"publish release"` -> `skills/deft-directive-release/SKILL.md` and cross-references the swarm Slack-announcement template. (7) Three-state exit codes (`0` success, `1` violation/refusal, `2` config error) match the conventions of `scripts/release.py`, `scripts/pr_check_protected_issues.py` (#702), and `scripts/rule_ownership_lint.py` (#705). Tests: 96 new tests across `tests/cli/test_release.py` (8 new for default-draft), `tests/cli/test_release_publish.py` (19), `tests/cli/test_release_rollback.py` (51), `tests/cli/test_release_e2e.py` (18) -- all use mocks on subprocess / gh / git helpers so CI never hits real GitHub. Encoding-safety pattern preserved: every file edit goes through Python `pathlib.Path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")`; PowerShell file edits use `--body-file` redirection for non-ASCII content. Closes #716. The companion `task release` foundation (Item below) closes #74; both discrete-task issues land in the same atomic PR per Repair Authority [AXIOM] (#709) so master is never in a release-without-rollback state.

- **feat(scripts,tasks,tests): `task release` automation -- changelog promote, roadmap move, tag, gh release** (#74, refs #233 More Determinism umbrella, refs #642 workflow umbrella, refs #635 epic anchor, refs #709 Repair Authority [AXIOM], refs #710 data-file-conventions check follow-up): Lands the deterministic encoding of the v0.X.Y release flow per #74. Three coordinated artifacts: (1) `scripts/release.py` -- argparse + pathlib + subprocess pipeline (`pre-flight git status` -> `pre-flight branch == master` -> `pre-flight CI` -> `CHANGELOG promotion` -> `ROADMAP refresh` -> `task build` -> `git tag -a vX.Y.Z` -> `git push origin vX.Y.Z` -> `gh release create vX.Y.Z`) with three-state exit codes (0 success / 1 violation / 2 config error) following the conventions of `scripts/pr_check_protected_issues.py` (#702) and `scripts/rule_ownership_lint.py` (#705). The `--dry-run` flag prints the full plan without writing files or invoking external commands; `--skip-tag` suppresses both `git tag` and `git push origin <tag>`; `--skip-release` suppresses `gh release create`; `--allow-dirty` bypasses the dirty-tree pre-flight (rehearsals only); `--repo OWNER/REPO` overrides the default resolution chain (`--repo` flag > `git remote get-url origin` parse > `deftai/directive` constant fallback). The CI step prefers `task ci:local` when present and falls back gracefully to `task check` when not -- the fallback exists because `task ci:local` is the sibling work item under the same #233 umbrella (in flight as agent2 in this swarm); both targets are detected via `task --list-all` regex match. CHANGELOG promotion is the single-source-of-truth pure function `promote_changelog(text, version, repo, today)`: locates the `## [Unreleased]` heading, renames it to `## [<version>] - <YYYY-MM-DD>`, inserts a fresh empty `## [Unreleased]` block (with the four canonical sub-sections) immediately above, rewrites the trailing `[Unreleased]:` link footer to `compare/v<version>...HEAD`, and appends a new `[<version>]: compare/v<previous>...v<version>` entry mirroring the existing footnote pattern (greenfield `releases/tag/v<version>` fallback when no previous version exists). ROADMAP move-to-completed delegates to the existing `task roadmap:render` (idempotent renderer aggregating `vbrief/pending/` Active + `vbrief/completed/` Completed) so vBRIEFs that should appear in `## Completed` are expected to have been moved via `task scope:complete` in advance -- the release script trusts the renderer rather than mutating ROADMAP.md directly. (2) `tasks/release.yml` -- new sub-Taskfile wrapping `uv run python {{.DEFT_ROOT}}/scripts/release.py {{.CLI_ARGS}}` with `dir: '{{.USER_WORKING_DIR}}'` (consumer-safe per #535) and `env: PYTHONUTF8: "1"` (#540 belt-and-suspenders); intentionally NO `sources:` / `generates:` per `conventions/task-caching.md` (#574) since `--dry-run` / `--skip-tag` / `--skip-release` / `--allow-dirty` / `--repo` are user-facing recovery flags that MUST NOT be silently dropped by go-task's incremental-build cache. The `release: ./tasks/release.yml` include is added to the root `Taskfile.yml` alongside the existing entries. (3) `tests/cli/test_release.py` -- 30+ tests using the in-process `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location` pattern from `tests/cli/test_pr_check_protected_issues.py` and `tests/cli/test_rule_ownership_lint.py`, covering `_validate_version` (parametrized valid + invalid), `_resolve_repo` (flag / https / ssh / failure / unparseable / git-missing), `promote_changelog` (heading rename, fresh Unreleased block, sub-sections preserved, compare link, Unreleased compare update, order preserved, greenfield, missing-Unreleased ValueError, idempotent), `_section_for_version`, `_split_body_and_links`, `task_has_target`, `run_ci` (prefers ci:local, falls back to check, neither, non-zero exit -- proves the **CI fallback** while `task ci:local` is in-flight), pipeline (dry-run no-writes, dirty-tree refused without `--allow-dirty` exit 1, dirty-tree accepted with the flag, wrong branch refused exit 1, `--skip-tag` suppresses git, `--skip-release` suppresses gh, CI failure exit 1, CHANGELOG missing exit 2, CHANGELOG-without-Unreleased exit 2), `main` (invalid version exit 2, missing positional argparse exit 2, `--help` exit 0, dry-run round-trip byte-identical), and a subprocess smoke test for `--help`. PowerShell encoding-safety pattern: every file edit goes through Python `pathlib.Path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")` -- no inline PS string ops on text containing non-ASCII. Closes #74. The pipeline now stages and commits CHANGELOG.md / ROADMAP.md (via `commit_release_artifacts`) BEFORE invoking `git tag -a vX.Y.Z`, then uses `git push --atomic origin <base-branch> vX.Y.Z` so the annotated tag and resulting GitHub release always anchor to the promoted commit and the working tree is clean post-pipeline (Greptile P1 review on PR #712 surfaced the missing-commit gap; the previous code would have tagged the pre-release HEAD and left a dirty tree).

- **feat(scripts,tasks,tests): `task ci:local` -- run the full CI pipeline locally (matrix-aware)** (#233 plan.item `task-ci-local`, refs #642 workflow umbrella, refs #635 epic anchor, refs #74 sibling sub-agent A `task release` PR, refs #709 Repair Authority [AXIOM], refs #633 pre-PR deterministic-CI enforcement umbrella, refs #710 data-file-conventions check follow-up): New `task ci:local` (Taskfile target in `tasks/ci.yml`, dispatches `uv run python {{.DEFT_ROOT}}/scripts/ci_local.py`) replicates the step graph of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` on the host platform so contributors catch CI failures before pushing -- mirrors the `python` job (uv sync + ruff + mypy tests/ + pytest --cov), the `go` job (go test ./cmd/deft-install/ + cross-compile builds for linux/amd64, darwin/arm64, windows/amd64), and the existing Taskfile-level verifications (`toolchain:check`, `verify:stubs`, `verify:links`, `verify:rule-ownership`, `vbrief:validate`, `build`); the Windows-only `windows-task-dispatch` regression pytest guard-rails are gated behind `--matrix=windows` AND a Windows host. New `scripts/ci_local.py` follows the argparse + pathlib + subprocess pattern of `scripts/rule_ownership_lint.py` (#705) and `scripts/pr_check_protected_issues.py` (#702): three-state exit codes (0 = every applicable step succeeded; 1 = at least one step failed; 2 = configuration error -- no applicable steps, missing root); flags `--matrix=<linux|macos|windows|all|host>` (default: host), `--skip-build` (skip cross-compile + `task build` + `task build:verify` for tight inner-loop iteration), `--verbose` (mirror CI logs verbatim, stream every step's stdout/stderr even on success), `--fail-fast` / `--no-fail-fast` (default fail-fast aborts the pipeline on the first failure; `--no-fail-fast` runs every applicable step and still reports a non-zero exit when any failed); per-step output of the form `[N/M] <step name>... OK (X.XXs)` / `FAIL` mirrors the GitHub Actions log style for debugging parity, with full stdout/stderr capture surfaced on failure (or always under `--verbose`); a final aggregate report prints total / passed / failed / skipped counts plus elapsed time and per-step diagnostics. The `task build:verify` step is detected at runtime via `task --list` and skipped with an informational message (not a failure) when missing -- it's a sibling pending #233 plan.item; once it lands the same `ci:local` invocation picks it up automatically. Per `conventions/task-caching.md` the new task forwards `{{.CLI_ARGS}}` to the script and intentionally declares no `sources:` / `generates:` so flags like `--skip-build` / `--no-fail-fast` are never silently swallowed by go-task's incremental-build cache. `Taskfile.yml` includes block gains a new `ci: ./tasks/ci.yml` (optional) entry, appended after `pr:` to keep the merge-cascade rebase against sibling sub-agent A's `release:` include addition mechanical (append-only ordering). Inline platform differences are documented in both `scripts/ci_local.py`'s module docstring and `tasks/ci.yml`'s top-of-file comment block: Linux/macOS use `/dev/null` as the cross-compile discard target; Windows uses `NUL`; Windows-task-dispatch regressions only run on a real Windows host because the steps shell out to PowerShell; per the existing PowerShell 5.1 encoding-safety pattern, the script writes nothing inline that requires non-ASCII string ops -- the on-disk artifacts (PR bodies, status files) are produced via `pathlib` / `create_file` and consumed via `--body-file` so multi-byte UTF-8 characters never round-trip through PowerShell's UTF-16LE internals. New `tests/cli/test_ci_local.py` (48 tests) loads `scripts/ci_local.py` in-process via `importlib.util` (registers the module in `sys.modules` before `exec_module` so the stdlib `@dataclass` introspection helpers can resolve `cls.__module__`) and covers: argument parsing for every flag including the mutually-exclusive `--fail-fast` / `--no-fail-fast` pair; host-matrix mapping (Linux/Darwin/Windows hosts plus the FreeBSD fallback); pipeline composition under each matrix and `--skip-build`; the `task build:verify` graceful-absence + present branches; the `windows-task-dispatch` row's gating on host AND matrix; runner OK/FAIL/SKIP behaviour including verbose stdout/stderr mirroring on success and the `--- stdout --- / --- stderr ---` diagnostic block on failure; fail-fast aborts subsequent steps with `aborted -- earlier step failed and --fail-fast is set` reasons; `--no-fail-fast` lets every step run; the `FileNotFoundError` path on a missing executable is surfaced as a fail row; aggregate-report counts and elapsed-time formatting; `main()` exit-code triplet (0 OK / 1 step failure / 2 config error); a synthetic round-trip that asserts the runner walks the expected step order and that the aggregate summary lands on stdout. Per acceptance criteria the umbrella issue #233 stays OPEN as the GitHub-side tracker for the 5 remaining pending items in the More Determinism vBRIEF (`vbrief/pending/2026-04-23-233-more-determinism-full-initiative-phase-0-spec.vbrief.json` -- Phase 0 generated per-phase gates, task doctor, build:verify, change:archive, task release); only the `task-ci-local` plan.item resolves with this PR.

- **feat(conventions,scripts,tasks): Rule Ownership Map data file + lint** (#635 ROM child, refs #642 workflow umbrella, refs #634 determinism-tier ladder T5/T6): Replaces the descriptive Rule Ownership Map prose section that PR #401 removed from `REFERENCES.md` with a structural data file plus deterministic lint enforcement, per the canonical [#642 workflow comment](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/642#issuecomment-4330742436) locked decision and the `## Rule Authority [AXIOM]` block in `main.md` (deterministic > Taskfile > vBRIEF > RFC2119 > prose). Three coordinated artifacts: (1) `conventions/rule-ownership.json` -- 47 ROM rows, each carrying `id` (slug), `text` (stable substring of the rule body), `owner_file` (path), `owner_section` (markdown heading), `authority` (`MUST`/`SHOULD`/`MUST_NOT`/`SHOULD_NOT`/`AXIOM`/`lesson`), and `last_verified` (ISO date). Coverage equals or exceeds the descriptive section Unit B removed: every original prose row is translated, plus additional load-bearing rules surfaced from `coding/coding.md` (modularity, contract-first, error-handling, quality checks), `coding/hygiene.md` (dead code, circular dependencies, error hiding, legacy code, DRY, comments), `coding/testing.md` (universal coverage, test-first), `coding/build-output.md`, `coding/toolchain.md`, `verification/verification.md` (stub detection, legacy detection), `core/glossary.md` (ubiquitous language, rule ownership principle, work decomposition hierarchy), `scm/git.md` (Conventional Commits, safety rules), `scm/github.md` (PR merge strategy, post-merge issue verification), `tools/taskfile.md`, `vbrief/vbrief.md` (lifecycle folders, filename convention), `resilience/continue-here.md`, `context/context.md`, `swarm/swarm.md`, `commands.md`, `main.md` (Rule Authority [AXIOM], vBRIEF persistence), `AGENTS.md` (Deft alignment confirmation, skill completion gate), 11 mainstream `languages/*.md` Hygiene sections, and 2 `meta/lessons.md` lesson-owned rules (`authority: lesson`, `owner_section: ## <lesson title>`); the `core/events.md` row from the original prose is intentionally omitted because that file was deleted by the PR #401 trim and respawned as event-wiring vBRIEFs under #635. (2) `scripts/rule_ownership_lint.py` -- argparse + pathlib + sys, follows the same conventions as `scripts/pr_check_protected_issues.py` (#701/#702): loads the data file, opens each `owner_file`, locates `owner_section` by exact ATX-heading match (level + text), extracts the section body up to the next equal-or-higher-level heading, and asserts the rule `text` substring is present. Exit codes: 0 = clean; 1 = drift detected (rule moved, section renamed, text rewritten -- diagnostic identifies which row, which file, and what was looked for); 2 = config error (data file missing, malformed JSON, schema violation, duplicate id, unknown authority). (3) New `verify:rule-ownership` task in `tasks/verify.yml` wraps the lint behind the canonical DEFT_ROOT pattern (mirrors `verify:stubs` / `verify:links`) and is wired as a dep of `task check` in `Taskfile.yml`, so any drift between the ROM data file and the owner files fails the pre-commit pipeline before merge. New `tests/cli/test_rule_ownership_lint.py` covers section extraction over varying heading levels and multi-section files, happy-path map/owner sync, drift detection (owner_file gone, owner_section renamed, rule text rewritten, rule moved between sections in the same file), the lesson-owner case (clean and drift), multiple-drift aggregation, the repository-wide smoke test asserting the real `conventions/rule-ownership.json` lints clean, and all five config-error branches (missing data file, malformed JSON, wrong shape, missing required field, invalid authority, duplicate id) -- 25 tests total. See `vbrief/proposed/2026-04-27-635-rule-ownership-map-data-file-and-lint.vbrief.json` for the scope vBRIEF.

- **docs(meta/lessons): codify GitHub closing-keyword false-positive lesson**: Appended a new `## GitHub Closing-Keyword False-Positive in Negation Context (2026-04)` section to `meta/lessons.md` capturing the #697 incident where issue #642 was auto-closed on squash merge despite the PR body intentionally avoiding `Closes`. Root cause: GitHub's closing-keyword parser is substring-based and matches `Closes #N` / `Fixes #N` / `Resolves #N` regardless of surrounding context (including negation parentheticals like "Intentionally not `Closes #642`"). Lesson includes (1) MUST NOT rule against writing closing keywords in negation/quotation/example contexts in PR bodies, (2) recommended alternative phrasings ("Intentionally NOT using a closing keyword for #N", `Refs #N (tracking umbrella; remains open)`), and (3) reinforcement that post-merge issue-state verification (#167's existing rule) catches both failure directions -- not just "should have closed but didn't" but also "should have stayed open but was auto-closed". Cross-references existing PR Merge Hygiene lesson #1 (#167), `scm/github.md`, and `skills/deft-directive-review-cycle/SKILL.md` Post-Merge Verification.

- **docs(skills,meta/lessons,tasks): codify Layer 3 closing-keyword false-positive (persistent GitHub-side `closingIssuesReferences` link)** (#701, refs #575, #633): Hardens the swarm/merge workflow against the third layer of the closing-keyword false-positive surfaced by workflow #642 -- two real incidents where umbrella issues auto-closed on squash merge despite the PR body being amended to `Refs #N` only (no closing keywords in the PR body, in commit messages, or in the explicit `--subject` / `--body-file` squash payload): PR #700 closed #233 (concatenated commit-message variant) and PR #401 closed #642 (persistent-link variant). Root cause: GitHub's `closingIssuesReferences` link is durable -- recorded the moment a closing keyword first appears in a PR body or an issue is attached via the Development sidebar, and survives every subsequent body / commit-message / squash-payload edit. **Primary encoding** lives in `skills/deft-directive-swarm/SKILL.md` Phase 6 Step 1 (per the Rule Authority [AXIOM] block in `main.md`, skill = RFC2119 with structured triggers is a stronger encoding than prose): added (1) a `!` (MUST) pre-merge `gh pr view <N> --json closingIssuesReferences` inspection rule that mandates manual unlinking via the PR's Development sidebar panel when a protected issue is GitHub-side linked, and (2) a `!` (MUST) post-merge protected-issue reopen sweep that runs `gh issue view` for each umbrella / staying-OPEN issue and `gh issue reopen` with a #701-citing comment on any auto-close regression. Added two Layer 3 ⊗ anti-patterns to the swarm SKILL Anti-Patterns block. **Secondary encoding (deterministic when invoked):** new `task pr:check-protected-issues` Taskfile target in `tasks/pr.yml` wrapping `scripts/pr_check_protected_issues.py`, which fetches `closingIssuesReferences` for a PR via `gh` and exits non-zero if any protected issue is linked (covered by `tests/cli/test_pr_check_protected_issues.py`). **Tertiary cross-reference:** short entry appended to `meta/lessons.md` (does NOT duplicate the rule body -- per [AXIOM] prose is fallback only; the entry exists for discoverability and explicitly cites #575 (lessons-consumption umbrella) and #633 (pre-PR deterministic-CI umbrella) as the consumption-gap context). Cross-linked `skills/deft-directive-review-cycle/SKILL.md` Post-Merge Verification with the inverse check (protected issues that auto-close MUST be reopened). Cross-references Layer 1 (#167), Layer 2 (#698), workflow umbrella (#642), incident PRs (#700, #401), and the canonical #642 workflow comment https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/642#issuecomment-4330742436. Closes #701.
